messages:
maya: heads up — new eval run with quantized-8bit + KV-cache warmup shows odd high BLEU variance on synthetic-augmented promptset. might be a seed thing, but only for the quantized runner.

oliver: can you paste the minimal repro and CI job id?

maya: repro steps in a sec. CI job: https://ci.internal/redwood/8472 — logs here: https://logs.internal/8472. quick snippet: 
```
# runner config
runner.seed: null  # we expected seed pinned
runner.kv_warmup: true
model.quantize: "int8"
```

sasha: hmm null seed is suspicious. synthetic augmentation relies on a deterministic shuffle. quant path might be reordering or invoking a different RNG path for kcache. did you check the shard seeding in runner.start()?

maya: noticed runner.start() calls `np.random.seed(seed or os.getpid())` for hosts without explicit seed — so when quantization toggles we spin up different worker processes and get different seeds. reproducible locally if you spawn multiple workers.

diego: that sounds like PYTHONHASHSEED / worker fork nondeterminism. our CI flakes before because the dataloader uses worker_init_fn that doesn't respect the runner-level seed.

lin: ci-bot says job 8472 failed tests: `eval-suite::synthetic_leakage_check` (3/10 failures).

ci-bot: [system] Job 8472: flaky test detected. See /artifacts/8472/summary.json

oliver: quick mitigation: force deterministic seeding at the process boundary and add a test that toggles quantize flag. patch idea: set runner.seed = int(seed) and in worker_init_fn do:
```python
def worker_init(worker_id):
    seed = base_seed + worker_id
    np.random.seed(seed)
    random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
```

sasha: also add an assert in the eval harness that synthetic augmentation order equals saved fixture when seed is pinned — that'll catch regressions early. metric we should fail on: leakage_rate > 0.01 for holdout prompts.

maya: I'll open a PR with the seed fix + unit that runs 5 repeats toggling quantize true/false to ensure bit-exact shuffle order. planning to include an integration CI job that pins workers.

diego: we should also audit `os.getpid()` usage — that's the main culprit for non-determinism when processes are reused by different configs.

lin: can we backfill recent eval runs to see when this started? maybe correlates with the KV warmup perf change deploy last week (deploy 2026-03-10).

maya: yes I'll run a quick historical pass across the eval index and post a small chart. if it lines up we'll revert the deploy on dedicated until patch lands.

oliver: thanks — prioritize the regression alert on the dashboard. sasha, can you add the alert rule? request: `eval.synthetic_leakage_rate > 0.01 over 5m` -> page oncall and open ticket.

sasha: on it. will also add a small CLI check `redwood-eval check-seed` that fails CI when seed isn't set.

maya: PR link once ready: https://git.internal/redwood/repo/pulls/2345 — contains patch + tests.

diego: once merged, add a CI job in the runner matrix that toggles quant flags and runs synthetic_leakage_check 3x to catch flakiness.

lin: thanks team. ping me if you need rollback help for the KV warmup deploy. :thumbsup:

maya: will do. this was fun to debug but want to lock it down before customer-facing benchmarks run next week. :slightly_smiling_face:
